correctness.rationale: The explicit 24-vertex coordinate/combinatorial graph construction is reproduced independently. All 13,874 nonempty independent faces are enumerated; a fully checked 6,934-pair discrete-Morse matching on 70,536 Hasse incidences is acyclic, leaving exactly one 0-cell, one 4-cell and four 5-cells. The signed integral Morse boundary is exactly the zero 1-by-4 matrix, not merely a mod-two matrix. Thus all four attachments S^4 to S^4 have degree zero and are nullhomotopic, yielding the stated S^4 wedge four S^5. A separate exact mod-two chain calculation agrees. Scope is precisely this finite graph.

evidence: Barmak, arXiv:1007.0418, Theorem 3.4 assumes a vertex in no triangle; every vertex of this graph lies in a triangle. His claw-free connectivity result is inapplicable to this graph, which contains induced claws; neither theorem lists the exact sphere multiplicities.

Goyal–Shukla–Singh, arXiv:1905.06926, Sections 3–5: product of complete graphs, generalized Mycielskian of complete graphs, and specified edge-replacement constructions. The present 24-vertex four-regular graph is none of the explicit product/Mycielski families.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The explicit relevant family theorems do not imply the displayed integral four- and five-dimensional sphere multiplicities. A 24-vertex four-regular graph cannot be K_m times K_n because degree (m-1)(n-1)=4 forces (m,n) in {(2,5),(3,3),(5,2)}, none with 24 vertices. A nontrivial generalized Mycielskian of K_n has nr+1 vertices; nr=23 and n>=2,r>=2 is impossible. The local edge-replacement theorem produces degree-three vertices absent here. A general method applicable in principle is not a pre-existing exact computation.

value.rationale: This is the exact integral homotopy type of the independence complex of a canonical 24-vertex, four-regular, vertex-transitive Archimedean polyhedron graph, rather than a manufactured graph or arbitrary parameter slice. Mixed dimensions four and five and their explicit minimal perfect Morse certificate have nontrivial topological content beyond face counts, graph parameters or generic connectivity estimates. It is a useful reproducible comparison object in graph-complex topology, with no speculative family theorem asserted.
